clauses.heading: 3. Onboarding a new supplier
clauses.text: 3.5 A supplier created in Bahi is ACTIVE from the day it is created, but no order may be placed with it until every document in §3.2 and, for food-contact parts, the certificate in §4 is on file.

clauses.heading: 4. Food-grade certificates
clauses.text: 4.1 A supplier of any part that comes into contact with food (gaskets, lids, body blanks, and any item marked food-contact in the item master) must hold a food-grade certificate. This is the certificate referred to in Purchase Policy §6.2.

clauses.heading: 4. Food-grade certificates
clauses.text: 4.5 An expired certificate counts as no certificate. The supplier stays ACTIVE in the master, but no food-contact part may be ordered from it until a new certificate is uploaded and checked.

clauses.heading: 4. Food-grade certificates
clauses.text: 4.2 The certificate must be a test report from a laboratory accredited for food-contact materials (for example an FSSAI-notified laboratory), or a BIS conformity certificate for stainless steel grade 304 or better.

clauses.heading: 1. What changes
clauses.text:
1.1 With effect from 1 December 2026, Purchase Policy POL-PUR-001 §3.3 is replaced by the following:

clauses.heading: 1. Purpose
clauses.text: This policy says how a supplier enters the supplier master in Bahi, what papers it must give us, when it is blocked, and how we stop the same supplier being registered twice. It sits under the Purchase Policy (POL-PUR-001 §6).

clauses.heading: 5. Approval limits
clauses.text: 5.2 The approval matrix (POL-APR-002) sets each role's limit. An order above the raiser's own limit must be approved by the next person up the line whose limit covers it.
